results.title: Archer to Shape Physical AI Future of Aerospace and Defense with Acquisition of Boeing’s Wisk Aero, Insitu and SkyGrid Subsidiaries - Insitu
highlights:
ARLINGTON, VA & SILICON VALLEY, CA, August 10, 2026 — The Boeing Company (NYSE: BA) and Archer Aviation Inc. (NYSE: ACHR) today announced the companies have signed definitive agreements in which Archer will acquire Boeing’s Wisk Aero, SkyGrid and Insitu subsidiaries. The deal will combine complementary capabilities developed over decades in autonomy, electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft, and unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) – creating a groundbreaking end-to-end physical AI platform for aerospace and defense.
...
In conjunction with the transaction, Boeing and Archer are entering into a collaboration and technology-sharing arrangement through which Boeing will retain access to the Wisk core autonomous flight technology for its current and next-generation commercial and defense aircraft. The transaction allows Boeing to retain strategic upside through its stake in Archer and simultaneously focus current and future investments into Boeing’s core businesses.
...
“This transaction is a win-win for Boeing and Archer,” said Brian Yutko, Boeing vice president, Commercial Airplanes Product Development. “It allows Wisk, SkyGrid and Insitu to accelerate capability development and time to market while ensuring Boeing capitalizes on its investments in these technologies over the past two decades through continued development in our core businesses. Having worked with the incredible teams in these companies firsthand, it’s clear this transaction will create an industry leader in the advanced aviation market. We look forward to collaborating with Archer to drive continued innovation in aerospace, defense and autonomy.”

On August 9, 2026, Archer Aviation Inc. (the “Company”) entered into a definitive Equity Purchase Agreement (the “Purchase Agreement”) with The Boeing Company (“Boeing”) to acquire all of the equity interests of Wisk Aero LLC, an autonomous aviation company, SkyGrid, LLC, a digital airspace integration and air traffic management platform, and Insitu, Inc., a manufacturer of unmanned aircraft systems and AI-enabled technologies, together with certain of their respective related entities, including Insitu Pacific Pty Ltd, Wisk Australia Pty Ltd, and Boeing Emirates Ltd (collectively, the “Target Companies”, and such acquisition, the “Acquisition”).

...
In conjunction with the transaction, Boeing and Archer are entering into a collaboration and technology-sharing arrangement through which Boeing will retain access to the Wisk core autonomous flight technology for its current and next-generation commercial and defense aircraft. The transaction allows Boeing to retain strategic upside through its stake in Archer and simultaneously focus current and future investments into Boeing's core businesses.
...
"This transaction is a win-win for Boeing and Archer," said Brian Yutko, Boeing vice president, Commercial Airplanes Product Development. "It allows Wisk, SkyGrid and Insitu to accelerate capability development and time to market while ensuring Boeing capitalizes on its investments in these technologies over the past two decades through continued development in our core businesses. Having worked with the incredible teams in these companies firsthand, it's clear this transaction will create an industry leader in the advanced aviation market. We look forward to collaborating with Archer to drive continued innovation in aerospace, defense and autonomy."

results.title: Archer to acquire Wisk Aero, SkyGrid and Insitu from Boeing - FlightGlobal
results.author: Ryan Finnerty
highlights:
# Archer to acquire Wisk Aero, SkyGrid and Insitu from Boeing
...
Advanced air mobility start-up Archer Aviation has reached a deal to acquire several emerging aerospace technology companies owned by Boeing.
...
The agreement covers electric aircraft developer Wisk, uncrewed aerial systems manufacturer Insitu and air traffic management solutions provider SkyGrid. Although the specific terms have not been disclosed, Archer says it has “signed definitive agreements” with Boeing covering the acquisitions.
...
An 8-K filing with US securities regulators on 9 August reveals that Boeing will take a nearly 20% ownership stake in Archer via stock transfer in exchange for the three companies. Additionally, Boeing will be granted warrants allowing it to purchase $200 million in Archer stock over the next several years at a fixed price.

results.title: Archer makes wild deal with Boeing swapping eVTOL startups for equity | Electrek
results.author: Fred Lambert
highlights:
Archer Aviation is buying three of Boeing’s aerospace subsidiaries: autonomous air-taxi developer Wisk Aero, military drone maker Insitu, and airspace-software firm SkyGrid. The deal also hands Boeing a stake in Archer.
...
Insitu is the prize. It’s a defense drone maker generating over $200 million in annual revenue, it’s profitable, and it has built more than 3,500 uncrewed aircraft systems fielded by the armed forces of 35 nations.
...
Financial terms weren’t disclosed. Boeing isn’t only selling here. It’s taking a stake in Archer and entering a technology-sharing collaboration, though no purchase price, investment amount, or equity percentage was announced. The deal is expected to close by the end of 2026, pending antitrust review.
...
Boeing kept its framing simpler. “This transaction is a win-win for Boeing and Archer,” said Brian Yutko, Boeing’s VP of Commercial Airplanes Product Development. “It allows Wisk, SkyGrid and Insitu to accelerate capability development and time to market.”
...
For a company that has burned cash for years chasing FAA certification, buying Insitu’s profitable, cash-generating business changes the entire company overnight. It steadies the balance sheet with real manufacturing and contracts, which until now were mostly a splashy unveiling and a stock pop.
